title: Bilingual storefront with full right to left support
narrative: As an Arabic first shopper, I want the entire store in Arabic with a correct right to left layout, so that I can buy without switching to a language I read less comfortably.
ac: English is the default language a visitor lands on, and is the canonical design
Given the store is in Arabic, every core page renders right to left with correct alignment, Arabic typography and spacing, and mirrored directional patterns where direction carries meaning
Given the store is in Arabic, no page breaks layout at any tested breakpoint on phone, tablet or desktop
Every core storefront function available in English is available in Arabic, with equivalent behaviour
Icons whose meaning depends on direction, such as back, forward and progress arrows, are mirrored in Arabic
Where content exists in only one language, the page renders without error and falls back predictably rather than showing an empty region

title: Language switcher
narrative: As any visitor, I want to change language from anywhere, so that I do not have to find my way back to the home page to do it.
ac: The switcher is present in the header on every page, including mobile
Given a visitor is on any page, when they switch language, then they arrive at the same page in the other language, not at the home page
The chosen language persists for the session and for a returning visitor on the same device
Given items are in the cart, when the language is switched, then the cart is unchanged

title: No hard coded storefront text
narrative: As the store owner, I want every word a customer reads to be translatable, so that neither language depends on a developer to correct a word.
ac: No string a customer can read is embedded in code
Every interface string, including validation and error messages, buttons, empty states and confirmation text, exists in both languages
A missing translation is visible in a report rather than silently rendering the other language

title: Locale aware formatting
narrative: As a shopper in either language, I want prices, numbers and dates to read naturally, so that the store does not look imported.
ac: Prices display in Egyptian Pounds throughout, with consistent decimal and thousands treatment
Dates and numbers follow the conventions of the active locale
The same order shows the same amount in both languages

title: Header and navigation
narrative: As a visitor, I want the header to give me search, my account, my wishlist and my cart wherever I am, so that I never have to hunt for them.
trace: NAV-01, NAV-03, NAV-04, NAV-05, NAV-06, NAV-07
ac: The header carries the logo, a prominent search bar, an account entry point, a wishlist entry point and a cart icon
The cart icon shows a live item count that updates when the cart changes, without a page reload
The mega menu and category navigation are driven by admin managed structure, not by code
Given the menu structure is changed in admin, when the storefront is reloaded, then the new structure appears

title: Mobile header and navigation
narrative: As a shopper on a phone, I want a header that does not consume the screen, so that I can see products.
ac: The mobile header is a simplified layout with quick search and a hamburger menu
The hamburger menu exposes the same category structure as the desktop mega menu
The mobile header behaves correctly in right to left

title: Trust and support pages
narrative: As a cautious buyer, I want to read the policies before I pay, so that I know what happens if the product is wrong.
trace: CMS-01 to CMS-08, CMS-10, IA-24 to IA-31
ac: The store carries About, Contact with a working form, Help and FAQ, Authenticity Guarantee, Shipping Policy, Return and Refund Policy, Privacy Policy, and Terms and Conditions
Each page exists in both languages and is reachable from the footer
The contact form delivers to the configured address and confirms submission to the sender
A WhatsApp click to chat link is present and opens a conversation with the configured number
The Return and Refund policy page states the return window configured in the system, so that policy and behaviour cannot drift apart

title: Premium visual treatment
narrative: As the store owner, I want discounting to look considered rather than cheap, so that the store reads as premium.
ac: Imagery, typography and spacing follow the approved Interface Design and its design system
Sale prices, savings and badges use the treatment defined in the design system, not a default theme treatment
The implemented pages match the approved design across all mobile and desktop states

title: Home page sections
narrative: As a first time visitor, I want the home page to show me what is worth buying, so that I do not have to know what to search for.
ac: The home page carries a hero banner or slider, trending products, new arrivals, featured collections, category shortcuts, brand highlights and promotional banners
Each section draws its products from the rule or curation set in admin, not from code
An empty section, for example no products currently flagged trending, renders without a broken region
Product cards link correctly to the product, and the `select_item` event fires

title: Trust signals and signup prompt
narrative: As a first time visitor, I want to see immediately that the store is genuine, so that I am willing to enter a card.
ac: Trust signals covering authenticity, delivery and returns appear on the home page
A newsletter or account signup prompt is present, and marketing consent is captured separately from the signup itself
The trust signal text is editable in admin in both languages

title: Home page content is editable
narrative: As the store owner, I want to change the home page myself, so that a campaign does not wait for a developer.
ac: Section content, images, links and calls to action are editable from admin without code
Given a section is edited and saved, when the storefront is reloaded, then the change is live
Each section is maintained independently in English and Arabic

title: Home page section order
narrative: As the store owner, I want to change what comes first, so that the page reflects the season rather than the build order.
ac: The order of existing home page sections can be changed from admin
Any section can be hidden and shown again without losing its content
The reduced boundary is explicit: section order and visibility are self service; **free form drag and drop composition with arbitrary new section types is not included**, per Annex A section 1.2

title: Product listing grid
narrative: As a visitor browsing a category, I want a grid that tells me price, availability and what is special about each product, so that I can compare without opening ten tabs.
trace: PLP-01 to PLP-05, PLP-17, PLP-20, PLP-21
ac: Each card shows image, name, price and any badge
A sale price is shown alongside the original price
Stock status is indicated on the card
Quick add to cart and quick add to wishlist work from the card without leaving the page
The result count is displayed, and the category banner, description and breadcrumb are shown
The `view_item_list` event fires with the list context

title: Filtering
narrative: As a visitor, I want to narrow a long list, so that I can reach a decision.
ac: Filters exist for category, brand, price range, attribute such as size or colour, and availability
Active filters are visible and each can be removed individually
Given filters are applied, when the visitor navigates to a product and returns, then the filters are still applied
On a phone, filters open in a dedicated drawer rather than pushing the results off screen
Filter labels and values are correct in both languages

title: Filter by rating
narrative: As a visitor, I want to see only well reviewed products, so that I can shortcut the decision.
ac: Delivered in the second release. All other filters are live at launch
Given ratings exist, when the rating filter is applied, then only products at or above the selected rating are returned

title: Sorting
narrative: As a visitor, I want to order the list the way I am shopping, so that the first screen is the useful one.
ac: Sorting is available by newest, price ascending, price descending, best selling and relevance
The chosen sort persists while filters are changed
Results are paginated or infinitely scrolled consistently, and the position is retained when returning from a product

title: Empty results
narrative: As a visitor whose filters returned nothing, I want a way forward, so that I do not leave.
ac: An empty result set shows an explanatory state, not a blank page
Alternative suggestions are offered, and the filters that produced no result can be cleared in one action
A zero result search records the term for later analysis and fires the zero result event

title: Search
narrative: As a visitor who knows what they want, I want to type it and find it, so that I do not have to learn the category tree.
ac: Search covers product name, description, SKU, brand and category
Suggestions appear as the visitor types
The results page carries the full filter set
Search operates correctly in both English and Arabic
The `search` event fires with the term and the result count

title: Arabic search handling
narrative: As an Arabic first shopper, I want my spelling to still find the product, so that I do not conclude the store does not stock it.
ac: A curated synonym and correction list covers the main categories and brands, including common Franco Arabic spellings
Given a term on the curated list, when it is searched in any of its listed forms, then the expected products are returned
The synonym list is managed from admin without a developer
The reduced boundary is explicit: **full automatic typo tolerance across the whole catalogue is not included**, per Annex A section 1.2. Coverage is what the curated list contains

title: Search term logging
narrative: As the store owner, I want to know what people searched for, so that I can stock what they wanted.
ac: Every search term is recorded with its result count
Zero result terms are distinguishable from terms that returned results
The reporting layer over this data is the search terms report, which is second release

title: Collection and brand pages
narrative: As a visitor following a campaign, I want a page that holds exactly the products it promised, so that the advertisement and the page agree.
ac: Curated collection pages and brand pages exist and are reachable from navigation and search
Products in a collection appear in the order set in admin
Each collection and brand page carries its own banner, description and imagery, maintained in both languages

title: Product media
narrative: As a visitor, I want to see the product properly, so that I am not guessing.
ac: The gallery supports multiple images with zoom
Video is supported where supplied
Media order follows the order set in admin
Images carry alt text, and a missing alt text is reported rather than silently absent

title: Product identity and price
narrative: As a visitor, I want the price and any saving stated plainly, so that I am not calculating.
ac: Product name and brand are shown
Price is shown, and where a sale price applies both the sale price and the original are shown with the saving
Price presentation follows the premium treatment in the design system, per MER-07

title: Variants and stock
narrative: As a visitor buying a specific size or colour, I want to know that exact option is available, so that I am not disappointed at checkout.
ac: Variant selection is available for the product attributes defined in admin
Stock status is shown per variant, not only per product
Given a variant is out of stock, when it is selected, then Add to Cart is unavailable for it and the reason is stated
The quantity selector cannot exceed the available stock of the selected variant

title: Add to cart, buy now and wishlist
narrative: As a visitor who has decided, I want to act immediately, so that the decision is not lost.
ac: Add to Cart adds the selected variant and quantity and confirms visibly
Buy Now takes the visitor to checkout with that item in the cart
Add to Wishlist works for a signed in customer and for a guest, per US-11-04
The `add_to_cart` and `add_to_wishlist` events fire with the correct item parameters

title: Product information
narrative: As a visitor, I want the description and specifications, so that I can confirm this is the right product.
ac: A short description or key features block appears above the fold on desktop
The full description is available on the page
A specifications table renders where specifications exist, and is absent rather than empty where they do not
All three are maintained independently in English and Arabic

title: Delivery, returns and authenticity
narrative: As a cautious buyer, I want to know when it arrives, what happens if I return it, and that it is genuine, before I add it to the cart.
scope: P1-L for the delivery estimate, otherwise P1
ac: A delivery estimate is shown where available for the customer location or the default zone
A returns policy summary is shown, consistent with the configured return window
An authenticity guarantee statement is shown and links to the authenticity page
The delivery estimate is presented as an estimate, and is not stated as a guaranteed date

title: Reviews on the product page
narrative: As a visitor, I want to read what other buyers said, so that I trust the listing.
ac: Approved reviews are displayed with the average rating
Only moderated and approved reviews appear
A product with no reviews shows a clean state, not an empty block
The reduced boundary is explicit: photo and video reviews, verified purchase badges, helpfulness voting and questions and answers are not included, per Annex A section 1.2

title: Related and recently viewed
narrative: As a visitor, I want to see near alternatives, so that a product that is not quite right does not end the visit.
ac: Related products are shown from the assignment made in admin
Recently viewed products are shown for the current visitor
Recently viewed persists for a signed in customer across sessions

title: Out of stock handling
narrative: As a visitor, I want to be told clearly that something is unavailable, so that I do not attempt to buy it.
ac: An out of stock product states so clearly on the product page
The product page, the cart and checkout are consistent about availability, with no route that results in an unintended sale
Given a product goes out of stock while it is in a cart, when the cart is viewed, then the customer is told before checkout
Back in stock notification signup is not included at launch, being P2

title: Sharing and structured data
narrative: As the store owner, I want product pages to be shareable and legible to search engines, so that marketing has something to work with.
ac: Share buttons are present and produce a correct link and preview
Product structured data is emitted and validates against the search engine testing tools
Structured data reflects the active language and the correct price and availability

title: Cart contents
narrative: As a shopper, I want to see exactly what I am buying, so that I can correct it before I pay.
ac: Each line shows image, name, selected variant, unit price and quantity
Quantity can be changed and the totals update
An item can be removed, and removal fires `remove_from_cart`
An item can be moved to the wishlist rather than deleted

title: Mini cart
narrative: As a shopper adding several items, I want to confirm each addition without leaving the page, so that browsing is not interrupted.
ac: Adding an item updates the header count and shows the mini cart
The mini cart lists current items and offers a route to the cart and to checkout
The mini cart renders correctly in right to left

title: Totals breakdown
narrative: As a shopper, I want every charge itemised, so that the final number is never a surprise.
ac: Subtotal, discount, shipping and total are shown separately
The total equals the sum of its parts, in both languages
Discounts never produce a negative order total

title: Free shipping progress
narrative: As a shopper one item away from free shipping, I want to be told, so that I add the item rather than abandon.
ac: Given one qualifying item is in the cart, when the cart is viewed, then it states that adding one more unlocks free shipping
Given two qualifying items are in the cart, when the cart is viewed, then shipping becomes free per the active promotion, with no code change required
The qualifying condition is read from the promotion configuration, not from code
The prompt disappears once the threshold is met

title: Cross sell in the cart
narrative: As the store owner, I want a relevant suggestion at the cart, so that average order value rises.
ac: Cart level cross sell suggestions are shown from the related product assignment
Adding a suggestion adds it to the same cart without losing the existing lines
The reduced boundary is explicit: automatic frequently bought together recommendation is P2

title: Coupon entry in the cart
narrative: As a shopper with a code, I want to know immediately whether it worked, so that I am not guessing at checkout.
ac: A valid coupon applies and the discount appears in the breakdown
Given an invalid, expired, exhausted or ineligible coupon, when it is entered, then a clear reason is shown and the total is unchanged
The reason distinguishes expired from ineligible from not found, in both languages
The `apply_coupon` event fires on a successful application

title: Stock re validation in the cart
narrative: As a shopper, I want the cart to tell me the truth about availability, so that checkout does not fail.
ac: Stock is re validated every time the cart is viewed
Given the available quantity has fallen below the cart quantity, when the cart is viewed, then the customer is told which line is affected and what quantity is available
The cart never permits progression to checkout with a quantity above available stock

title: Empty cart
narrative: As a shopper with an empty cart, I want somewhere to go, so that the visit is not over.
ac: The empty cart shows an explanatory state with suggestions
The suggestions link to live, in stock products

title: Cart persists for signed in customers
narrative: As a returning customer, I want my cart to be where I left it, on whatever device I pick up, so that I do not rebuild it.
ac: Given a signed in customer adds items on one device, when they sign in on another device, then the same cart is present
The cart survives sign out and sign in
Prices are re validated when the cart is restored, and a changed price is shown as changed rather than applied silently

title: Guest cart survives registration
narrative: As a guest who filled a cart and then decided to register, I want to keep everything I chose, so that registering does not cost me my basket.
ac: Given a guest cart with items, when the guest completes registration, then every item is present in the new account cart
No item is lost and no quantity is changed
The behaviour holds whether registration is started from the cart, the header or the checkout

title: Guest cart merges on sign in
narrative: As a guest who filled a cart and then signed in, I want both carts combined sensibly, so that I lose nothing and see no duplicates.
ac: Given a guest cart and a saved account cart both containing items, when the guest signs in, then the two merge into one cart
No item from either cart is lost
The same product and variant appearing in both carts produces one line, not two
Given merging would exceed available stock for a line, when the merge occurs, then the quantity is capped at available stock and the customer is told what changed
Prices are re validated on merge

title: Guest cart survives Google sign in
narrative: As a guest signing in with Google, I want identical cart behaviour, so that the faster route is not the lossy one.
ac: The merge behaviour in US-05-11 holds identically through the Google flow
Given the Google account email matches an existing account, when sign in completes, then the cart merges into that existing account and no second account is created

title: Guest cart survives a browser close
narrative: As a guest who came back tomorrow, I want my cart still there, so that I can finish what I started.
ac: A guest cart survives closing and reopening the browser within the defined retention window
The retention window is a documented setting, not a hard coded value
Stock and prices are re validated when the cart is restored

title: Register with email and password
narrative: As a new customer, I want to create an account quickly, so that I am not filling a form before I have bought anything.
ac: Registration requires no more than email, password and consent. No unnecessary mandatory fields
Email verification is sent and the account state reflects whether the email is verified
Marketing consent is captured separately from account creation, and is not implied by registering
The `sign_up` event fires
Phone number registration is available at the reduced scope recorded at AUTH-02

title: Sign in and password reset
narrative: As a returning customer, I want to get back in without friction, so that I buy rather than give up.
ac: Sign in with email and password succeeds and fires the `login` event
A failed sign in states that the credentials are wrong without revealing whether the email exists
Password reset sends a link that is single use and time limited, and a used or expired link says so plainly
A passwordless email sign in link is available as an alternative, at the scope recorded at AUTH-12

title: Sign in and register with Google
narrative: As a visitor who does not want to invent another password, I want to use my Google account, so that I can buy in one tap.
ac: A visitor can both register and sign in with a Google account
Given no account exists for the Google email, when sign in completes, then an account is created and the customer is signed in
Given an account already exists for that email, when sign in completes, then the customer is signed in to it and no second account is created
The cart merge in US-05-12 applies
Social login beyond Google is not in the first release, being P2

title: One account per email
narrative: As the store owner, I want one customer to be one record, so that order history, returns and marketing are not split across duplicates.
ac: Given an account created by Google sign in, when the same email registers manually, then the two resolve to one account rather than creating a second
Given an account created manually, when that email signs in with Google, then the existing account is used
The resolution is explained to the customer rather than failing silently
No route through registration, guest checkout linking or Google sign in produces two accounts for one email address

title: Account security
narrative: As the store owner, I want accounts to be difficult to attack, so that a breach is not the first thing customers hear about us.
ac: Sessions are handled securely and expire per the documented policy
Login attempts are rate limited, and the limit is a documented setting
Automated account creation is protected against
Passwords are stored using current secure practice, and are never recoverable in readable form

title: Guest checkout
narrative: As a cautious buyer, I want to buy without an account, so that a purchase does not become a commitment.
ac: A purchase completes end to end with no account created and no forced registration step
Registration is encouraged, not required, and the encouragement does not obstruct the guest route
The guest receives the same order confirmation and the same notifications as a registered customer

title: One step account creation after ordering
narrative: As a guest who has just ordered, I want to become a customer by choosing a password, so that I do not retype everything I just entered.
ac: The order confirmation offers account creation requiring a password only
Given the guest sets a password, when the account is created, then name, email, phone and address are carried across with no re entry
The order just placed is linked to the new account and appears in order history
The linking is secure: a guest order cannot be claimed by an account that does not own the ordering email
Declining the offer leaves the order intact and reachable through the confirmation email

title: Address entry and saved addresses
narrative: As a customer, I want to give my address in the form Egyptian couriers actually use, so that the parcel arrives.
ac: The address form captures governorate, city, district, street and landmark
Governorate is selected from the list the shipping zones are configured against, not typed freely
A returning customer selects from saved addresses rather than retyping
Validation errors name the field and the problem, in both languages
Address autocomplete via maps is not in the first release, being P2

title: Shipping method and cost
narrative: As a customer, I want to know the delivery cost before I commit, so that the total is not a surprise.
ac: The shipping cost is calculated from the manual rate zone matching the selected governorate
A delivery estimate is shown where available
Given a free shipping promotion applies, when the total is calculated, then the shipping charge is overridden to zero
Given no rate zone matches the address, when the customer reaches this step, then the checkout states the problem rather than charging zero silently

title: Payment method selection
narrative: As a customer, I want to pay the way I prefer, so that I do not abandon at the last step.
scope: P1, with method availability conditional on OD-05 and OD-19
ac: The methods offered are exactly those enabled in configuration and approved for the merchant account
Card payment with 3-D Secure authentication is available
Cash on delivery appears only if it is selected and configured, including any value limit, zone restriction or fee
Mobile wallet appears only if selected and approved by the provider
Disabling a method in configuration removes it from checkout without a code change

title: Order review and terms
narrative: As a customer, I want one last look before I pay, so that I catch my own mistake.
ac: A review step shows items, address, shipping method, payment method and the full total breakdown before confirmation
An order notes field is available
Terms acceptance is required and is recorded against the order
Every charge in the breakdown is itemised, with no unexplained difference between the review total and the amount charged

title: Coupon at checkout
narrative: As a customer who found a code late, I want to apply it at checkout, so that I do not have to go back to the cart.
ac: A coupon can be entered at checkout with the same validation and messaging as the cart
An invalid coupon leaves the total unchanged and states the reason
Applying a coupon recalculates shipping where the coupon affects it

title: Stock validation at placement
narrative: As the store owner, I want an order never to be confirmed for stock we do not have, so that we do not sell what we cannot ship.
ac: Stock is re validated at the moment Place Order is pressed, not only when the cart was viewed
Given stock ran out between the cart and placement, when the order is placed, then the unavailable quantity is not confirmed and the customer is informed before payment is taken
The customer is told exactly which line is affected and what quantity is available
No order is created in a state that reserves more stock than exists

title: Duplicate order and duplicate charge protection
narrative: As the store owner, I want a double click to be harmless, so that we never charge twice or ship twice.
ac: Given Place Order is pressed twice in rapid succession, when the requests are processed, then exactly one order is created and exactly one charge is made
Given the payment provider sends the same confirmation callback twice, when both are received, then the second has no additional effect on the order, the stock or the payment record
The protection holds across a page refresh and a back button during payment
The duplicate attempt is recorded so it can be diagnosed, rather than silently discarded

title: Order confirmation
narrative: As a customer who has just paid, I want proof and a next step, so that I know it worked.
ac: The confirmation shows the order number, an item summary, the amount charged and an estimated delivery
The confirmation is reachable again from the confirmation email
The `purchase` event fires with items, tax, shipping and discount values
For a guest, the one step account creation offer in US-06-07 is presented here

title: Mobile checkout
narrative: As a shopper on a phone, I want checkout to be short, so that I finish it standing up.
ac: Every checkout step is usable on a phone without horizontal scrolling
Input types match the field, so that numeric and telephone keyboards appear where appropriate
The mobile checkout is correct in right to left

title: Order status model
narrative: As the store owner, I want order state to be explicit and complete, so that the system never has to guess what happened.
ac: The status set is Pending Payment, Payment Failed, Confirmed, Preparing, Shipped, Out for Delivery, Delivered, Cancelled, Delivery Failed or Returned to Origin, COD Collected Awaiting Remittance, Return Requested, Return Approved or Rejected, Returned, and Refund Pending, Refunded or Partial
Delivery Failed or Returned to Origin is a distinct state and is never recorded as Delivered
Invalid transitions are rejected with a clear message rather than silently accepted
Every status change records who made it and when

title: Payment abstraction layer
narrative: As the store owner, I want the payment provider to be replaceable, so that a commercial decision does not become a rebuild.
ac: Checkout talks to an internal payment interface, not directly to the provider
The provider integration sits behind an adapter with retries, logging and webhook handling
Changing provider requires a new adapter, not changes to the checkout flow
Integration failures are logged with enough detail to diagnose them

title: No card data on Mizzey servers
narrative: As the store owner, I want card data never to touch our systems, so that our compliance burden stays small.
ac: Payment uses the provider hosted and tokenised flow
No card number, expiry or security code is stored, logged or transmitted by the store
The stored payment record holds a transaction reference and status, never card data

title: Callback verification
narrative: As the store owner, I want a payment confirmation to be provably genuine, so that nobody can mark an order paid by forging a request.
ac: Every payment callback is cryptographically verified before it is acted upon
Given a callback fails verification, when it is received, then it is rejected, logged, and has no effect on the order
Verification failures are visible to the team rather than only in a log file

title: Payment failure handling
narrative: As the store owner, I want a failed payment to leave the order unmistakably unpaid, so that we never ship against a failure.
ac: Given a payment fails, when the result is processed, then the order is set to Payment Failed and is never shown as Paid or Confirmed
Reserved stock is released per the reservation policy
The customer receives a payment failed notification with a retry route
A retry that succeeds moves the same order forward rather than creating a second one

title: Payment records
narrative: As the accountant, I want every payment traceable to its provider transaction, so that reconciliation is possible.
ac: Transaction reference, status, amount, currency and timestamps are stored against the order
The distinction between paid and funds received is recorded and documented
The Accountant role can read payment records and transaction references
A role without financial permission cannot reach them

title: Refunds
narrative: As the accountant, I want to refund from the order screen, correctly and only once, so that a refund is never larger than the payment.
ac: A full refund can be issued from the order screen through the provider
A partial refund can be issued for a specified amount or specified items
Given discounts were applied, when a refund is attempted, then it cannot exceed the amount actually paid for that item or order after discount
Given a staff member without refund permission, when they open the order, then the refund action is not available to them
Every refund records amount, status, payment reference, actor and timestamp, and is written to the audit log
The refund event fires for analytics

title: Cash on delivery capability
narrative: As the store owner, I want cash on delivery built and tested, so that turning it on is a decision rather than a project.
ac: Cash on delivery is implemented and tested whether or not it is enabled at launch
Enabling or disabling it is a configuration change, including any value limit, zone restriction or fee
A cash on delivery order moves to COD Collected Awaiting Remittance on collection, distinct from funds received
Cash on delivery verification by one time password is not in the first release, being P2, and is an open decision at OD-29

title: Shipping zones and rates
narrative: As the store owner, I want to set delivery prices by governorate myself, so that a rate card change is not a developer task.
ac: Shipping zones and their rates are managed from admin
Zones are configured by governorate, matching the client carrier rate card
Changing a rate takes effect on the next checkout calculation without a code change
Every governorate the store ships to has a rate, and a gap is reported rather than defaulting to zero

title: Carrier integration
narrative: As the warehouse, I want orders to reach the carrier from the order screen, so that we are not retyping addresses into another system.
ac: An order is pushed to the carrier and a tracking code returns automatically and is linked to the order
The integration sits behind an adapter with retries, logging and webhook handling
Given the carrier is unreachable, when a dispatch is attempted, then the failure is reported to the operator and the order is not falsely marked shipped

title: Bulk dispatch, labels and pickups
narrative: As the warehouse, I want to send the day in one action, so that dispatch is minutes rather than hours.
ac: Many orders can be sent to the carrier in one action
Airway bills for the dispatched selection print together
Pickup requests are created and their state is tracked

Given some orders in a bulk dispatch fail, when the action completes, then the successes are recorded, the failures are listed individually with reasons, and the operation is safe to retry for the failures only

title: Carrier status retrieval
narrative: As the store owner, I want the order to show where the parcel is, so that customers do not have to ask.
ac: Carrier status is retrieved and reflected on the order
The customer sees the current status in their account and through the tracking link
A stale or missing carrier status is shown as unknown rather than as a false state

title: Explicit carrier status mapping
narrative: As the store owner, I want to know exactly how a carrier status becomes an order status, so that a carrier quirk does not corrupt our records.
ac: The mapping from every carrier status to an order status is explicit, documented, and visible in admin
An unrecognised carrier status does not change the order status, and is raised for a human decision
The mapping is verified against real carrier responses during Stage 4, not assumed from documentation

title: Returned to origin is never Delivered
narrative: As the store owner, I want an undelivered parcel recorded as undelivered, so that an unpaid return is never counted as a completed sale.
ac: Given a parcel is returned to origin, when the carrier reports it, then the order is recorded as Delivery Failed or Returned to Origin
The order is never recorded as Delivered in this case, under any carrier status mapping
Stock state and payment state remain correct: nothing is treated as sold and no payment state is advanced
The case appears in the operations queue for a decision

title: Cash on delivery reconciliation
narrative: As the store owner, I want collected money and received money kept apart, so that the dashboard never overstates my cash position.
ac: Collected and remitted are recorded separately per order
An order delivered against cash on delivery shows as collected but not remitted until remittance is recorded
The difference between collected and remitted is visible as a figure, not only as two lists
The remittance cycle used is the one the client confirms under OD-20

title: Account dashboard
narrative: As a returning customer, I want one place that holds my orders, addresses and returns, so that I am not hunting.
ac: The dashboard shows an overview with routes to profile, addresses, orders, wishlist and returns
Recent orders are shown with their current status
A customer sees only their own data, verified by attempting access to another customer record

title: Order history, detail and tracking
narrative: As a customer, I want to see exactly what I was charged and where the parcel is, so that I do not have to ask.
ac: Order history lists all orders with number, date, total and status
Order detail shows the full breakdown as charged, including items, discounts, shipping and payment method
Given a price changed after the order, when the order is viewed, then it still shows the price originally charged
Tracking shows the current carrier status where a shipment exists

title: Invoice download
narrative: As a customer, I want a document I can file, so that I can claim or account for the purchase.
ac: An invoice can be downloaded from the order
The invoice carries the legal entity details supplied under CR-12 and the tax treatment settled under OD-09
The invoice reflects the amounts actually charged, including discounts

title: Address book
narrative: As a customer, I want my addresses saved, so that ordering again is fast.
ac: Addresses can be added, edited, deleted and set as default
The default address is pre selected at checkout
Deleting an address does not alter the address recorded on past orders

title: Profile and password
narrative: As a customer, I want to correct my own details, so that a typo is not permanent.
ac: Profile details are editable and the change is confirmed
Password change requires the current password and confirms success
Changing the email requires verification of the new address

title: Reorder
narrative: As a returning customer, I want to repeat a previous order, so that a routine purchase takes one action.
ac: Delivered in the second release. At launch, customers can view past orders and add items manually
Given a past order, when reorder is used, then a cart is built from its items subject to current availability and current prices
Items no longer available are reported rather than silently omitted

title: Account deletion request
narrative: As a customer, I want to ask for my account to be removed, so that I am not stuck in a system I have left.
ac: Delivered in the second release. At launch, deletion requests are handled manually on request
A request is recorded with a timestamp and is visible to the team
Handling respects the record retention the client is obliged to keep for completed orders

title: Submit a review
narrative: As a customer who received a product, I want to say what I thought, so that other buyers are better informed.
ac: A star rating and written text can be submitted
The submission is acknowledged and its pending state is explained
The reduced boundary is explicit: photo and video reviews, verified purchase badges, helpfulness voting and questions and answers are not included

title: Review moderation
narrative: As the store owner, I want to approve reviews before they publish, so that the store is not a channel for abuse.
ac: No review is publicly visible before approval
A moderator can approve or reject, and rejection is recorded
The average rating shown on the product page and listing counts approved reviews only

title: Review invitation
narrative: As the store owner, I want to ask for reviews after delivery, so that the catalogue accumulates proof.
ac: A review invitation is sent after delivery is recorded
The invitation is subject to the notification consent rules
The invitation links directly to the review form for the delivered product

title: Wishlist
narrative: As a shopper who is not ready to buy, I want to save the product, so that I can find it again.
ac: Items can be added to and removed from the wishlist from the product page and the listing card
The wishlist persists for a signed in customer
A guest gets a temporary wishlist for the session
The reduced boundary is explicit: sharing, multiple lists and price drop alerts are not included

title: Move wishlist to cart
narrative: As a shopper who has decided, I want to move a saved item into the cart, so that the save was useful.
ac: An item moves from wishlist to cart in one action
An out of stock wishlist item cannot be moved to the cart, and the reason is stated

title: Guest wishlist transfers on sign in
narrative: As a guest who saved items and then signed in, I want to keep them, so that the save was not wasted.
ac: Given a guest wishlist, when the guest registers or signs in, then the items transfer to the account wishlist
An item already saved to the account does not duplicate

title: Recently viewed
narrative: As a shopper comparing options, I want to get back to what I just looked at, so that I do not lose the shortlist.
ac: Recently viewed products are shown to the visitor
The list persists across sessions for a signed in customer
Product comparison is not included, being P2

title: Account created notification
narrative: As a new customer, I want a welcome that confirms my account and my discount, so that I know registration worked.
ac: A welcome email is sent containing verification and, where the welcome discount applies, its details and conditions
The email renders correctly in both languages and in common email clients
The language of the email matches the language the customer used

title: Order confirmation notification
narrative: As a customer, I want written confirmation of what I ordered, so that I have a record.
ac: An order confirmation email is sent containing the order number and a summary
It is sent for guest orders as well as account orders
It carries a route back to the order confirmation page

title: Payment failed notification
narrative: As a customer whose payment failed, I want to know and be able to retry, so that the order is not simply lost.
ac: A payment failed email is sent with a retry route
It does not state or imply that the order is confirmed

title: Shipping and delivery notifications
narrative: As a customer, I want to know when it ships and when it arrives, so that I can be there.
ac: A shipped email is sent with the carrier and the tracking number
A delivered email is sent with a review invitation
An out for delivery update is not in the first release, being P2

title: Return update notifications
narrative: As a customer who requested a return, I want to be told each time it moves, so that I am not chasing it.
ac: An email is sent when a return is approved, rejected or received
A rejection states the recorded reason

title: Refund notification
narrative: As a customer, I want confirmation of my refund and its reference, so that I can match it to my statement.
ac: A refund completed email is sent with the amount and the payment reference
A partial refund states the amount refunded and what it covers

title: Consent, frequency and compliance
narrative: As the store owner, I want sending governed by consent, so that marketing activity stays inside the law.
trace: NOTF-11, NOTF-12, NOTF-13, AUTH-09, NFR-12, R-04
ac: Transactional email is separated from marketing email, and marketing sending requires recorded consent
Frequency limits are respected
Sending complies with the email provider policies, and unsubscribe is present on marketing email
Consent state is visible against the customer record
A notification preferences page is second release; unsubscribe links serve at launch

title: Notification templates
narrative: As the store owner, I want to change the wording of emails myself, so that tone is not a developer task.
ac: Delivered in the second release. At launch, the developer changes email wording on request
Templates are editable in both languages
A template edit cannot break the variables the email depends on

title: Request a return
narrative: As a customer with a product that is wrong, I want to start the return myself, so that I do not have to negotiate by message.
ac: A return is requested from the account, against a specific order
The request captures the item, the quantity, a reason from a defined list, and a free text description
Photographs can be attached optionally
The request is confirmed on screen and by email
The `return_request` event fires

title: Return eligibility
narrative: As the store owner, I want the return window enforced automatically, so that the policy is applied consistently.
ac: Eligibility is checked automatically against the configured return window
Given an order outside the window, when a return is attempted, then it is refused with the reason and the window stated
The window is a configuration value, and the policy page states the same value
The reduced boundary is explicit: a complex per product or per category eligibility rule engine is not included

title: Return status visibility
narrative: As a customer, I want to see where my return is, so that I am not left wondering.
ac: The customer sees the return status at every stage from their account
The stages shown match the states the team works through
A rejected return shows the recorded reason

title: Refund visibility
narrative: As a customer, I want to see that the refund was issued and to what, so that I know where to look for the money.
ac: The refund state is visible on the order and the return
The amount and the destination, being the original payment method, are stated
Where settlement takes time, the timing is explained rather than left ambiguous

title: Promotion engine
narrative: As the store owner, I want to build an offer myself, so that a campaign does not need a release.
trace: PROMO-01 to PROMO-19, PROMO-23, FIX-08, ADM-110, ADM-111, ADM-113, ADM-115, ENT-11
scope: P1, with stacking, priority and customer group at P1-L
ac: Reward types available are percentage discount, fixed amount discount and free shipping
Conditions available are minimum cart value, minimum item count, specific products, specific categories, specific brands, first order only, and customer group
A promotion can be automatic with no code, or require a coupon code
Usage limits can be set in total and per customer
Start and end dates can be scheduled, and a promotion can be paused or deactivated without deleting its usage history
Product and category exclusions and a maximum discount cap can be set
Every one of the above is configured from admin with no code change
Buy X get Y, tiered discounts and bundle pricing are not included, being P2

title: Welcome discount
narrative: As the store owner, I want a welcome discount that applies only where it should, so that it drives registration without leaking margin.
ac: Value, cap, expiry and eligibility are all configurable from admin
Given a new customer meets the configured conditions, when they check out, then the discount applies
Given the conditions are not met, when they check out, then the discount does not apply and the reason is available
The discount cannot be used more times than its configured limit

title: Free shipping rule
narrative: As the store owner, I want free shipping to follow a rule I set, so that I can change the threshold without a developer.
ac: The qualifying condition is admin configurable
Given the condition is met, when totals are calculated, then the free shipping promotion overrides the calculated shipping rate
Changing the threshold takes effect without a code change

title: Promotion stacking is explicit
narrative: As the store owner, I want to control which offers combine, so that a customer never accidentally receives three discounts at once.
scope: P1 for the rule, P1-L for the configuration depth
ac: Whether the welcome discount, a coupon and free shipping can combine is a setting, not a hidden behaviour
Where two promotions compete, the configured priority decides which applies
The applied promotions are itemised in the totals breakdown so the customer and the team can see what was applied
Given stacking is disallowed, when a second promotion is attempted, then the customer is told which one applied and why the other did not

title: Price snapshot
narrative: As the store owner, I want a past order to keep its own prices forever, so that changing a price today never rewrites history.
ac: Every order item stores the price charged at the moment of order, together with the discount applied
Given a product price is changed, when a prior order is viewed, then it shows the original price
Reports, invoices and refunds all use the snapshot, not the current price

title: Refund integrity
narrative: As the store owner, I want the system to make an over refund impossible, so that a mistake cannot cost more than the sale.
ac: A refund cannot exceed the amount actually paid for that item or order after discounts
Cumulative partial refunds cannot exceed the same limit
An attempt to exceed it is refused with a clear message, and the attempt is logged

title: Stock returns on cancellation
narrative: As the store owner, I want cancelled orders to release their stock, so that the catalogue does not show as sold out when it is not.
ac: A cancelled order releases its stock back under the agreed reservation policy
A failed payment releases reserved stock under the same policy
The reservation policy is documented, including how long stock is held for an unpaid order

title: No negative totals
narrative: As the store owner, I want discounts never to produce a negative total, so that no combination of offers can pay a customer to order.
ac: Given any combination of promotions, when totals are calculated, then the order total is never below zero
Where a discount would exceed the order value, it is capped at the order value

title: Merchandising controls
narrative: As the store owner, I want to promote specific products without editing code, so that merchandising is a daily activity.
trace: MER-01 to MER-05, ADM-42, ADM-43, SSC-22, SSC-23
ac: Badges of New, Trending, Limited and Best Seller can be assigned per product
A product can be flagged featured, and the flag affects home page and collection prominence
Products can be ordered manually within categories and collections
Related products can be assigned per product

title: The Operations Console
narrative: As the store owner, I want one page that tells me what needs doing today, so that nothing is missed because it lived on a different screen.
ac: A dedicated admin landing page combines the outstanding work of the day in one view
The page is organised around jobs to be done, not around database entities
Quick actions can be performed from the console without navigating away
The console respects the role of the person viewing it, showing only what that role may act on

title: Orders requiring action queue
narrative: As the warehouse, I want a work queue I can clear top to bottom, so that I know when the day is done.
ac: The queue contains new, unpaid, ready to dispatch and failed delivery orders
The queue is ordered so it can be worked top to bottom
Acting on an order removes it from the queue without a manual refresh
A returned to origin order appears here for a decision, per US-09-06

title: Stock requiring attention
narrative: As the store owner, I want to see catalogue problems before customers do, so that we are not selling what we cannot ship or hiding what we can.
ac: The panel shows low stock, out of stock, products missing an image, and unpublished products
Each entry links directly to the product for correction
The low stock threshold used is the one configured per SKU or globally

title: Today summary
narrative: As the store owner, I want the day in four numbers, so that I know without running a report.
ac: Today orders, revenue, units and pending dispatch are shown
Revenue shown is consistent with the sales report for the same period
Where cash on delivery is in use, collected is not presented as received, per US-09-07

title: Saved views
narrative: As the store owner, I want to save a filtered list I use daily, so that I am not rebuilding the same filter every morning.
ac: Any filtered list can be saved and reopened in one click
Saved views belong to the user who created them
A saved view whose filter is no longer valid explains itself rather than erroring

title: Add a product in under three minutes
narrative: As the store owner, I want adding a simple product to be genuinely quick, so that new stock goes live the day it arrives.
ac: A simple product with title, price, stock, image and category can be created and published in under three minutes by a trained operator
The three minute figure is measured during the Stage 4 gate by the client team, not by the developer
An existing product can be duplicated as a starting point
Required fields are the minimum needed to publish, and optional fields do not block saving

title: Inline edit grid
narrative: As the store owner, I want to change price and stock across many products on one screen, so that a price update is one task rather than fifty.
ac: Price and stock are editable across many products on one screen, without opening each product
Changes are saved together and reported as a set, with any failures listed individually
Every change is written to the price and stock change history with user and timestamp
The reduced boundary is explicit: **full spreadsheet style editing of every field is not included**, per Annex A section 1.2. The grid covers price and stock

title: Bulk order operations
narrative: As the warehouse, I want to act on many orders at once, so that dispatch scales with volume.
scope: P1, with carrier dispatch and label printing at P1-L
ac: Order status can be changed in bulk, with invalid transitions rejected per order rather than failing the whole action
Many orders can be dispatched to the carrier at once, with airway bills printed together
Packing slips can be printed in bulk
A partial failure reports exactly which orders failed and why, and is safe to retry for those only

title: Bulk product operations
narrative: As the store owner, I want to change many products at once, so that a seasonal change is not a week of clicking.
scope: P1, with category assignment and combined bulk update at P1-L
ac: Price can be changed by amount or percentage across a selection
Stock can be set or adjusted across a selection
Products can be published, unpublished or archived in bulk
Products can be assigned to a category in bulk
Every bulk change is written to the audit log as one action with its affected set

title: Find anything quickly
narrative: As the team, I want to find a product or an order in seconds, so that a customer on the phone is not waiting.
ac: Any product is found by SKU, title or barcode
Any order is found by customer phone number
Orders are also searchable by order number, customer name, email, status, payment state, date and carrier
Search returns results in a time the client team accepts during the Stage 4 gate

title: Admin language and mobile use
narrative: As the team, I want a consistent admin in one language and usable on a phone for quick checks, so that training is simple and the shop floor is not tied to a desk.
scope: P1, with mobile admin at P1-L
ac: The administrative interface is in English, consistently across standard screens and the custom Operations Console
The admin is usable on a mobile device for order status checks and stock updates
The administrator guide and the training session are delivered in Arabic, covering the English interface
An Arabic administrative interface is not included, being P2

title: Product lifecycle
narrative: As the store owner, I want to create, change, clone and retire products, so that the catalogue reflects what we actually sell.
ac: Products can be created, edited, archived and cloned
Draft, published and scheduled states are supported
An archived product disappears from the storefront but remains on past orders
A scheduled product publishes at its scheduled time without intervention

title: Every product field is editable
narrative: As the store owner, I want to change any part of a product myself, so that I never wait for a developer to fix a description.
trace: SSC-20, ADM-22 to ADM-27, ADM-29 to ADM-45, SSC-29
scope: P1, with compare at price, weight and dimensions, tax class and shipping flags at P1-L
ac: Name, description, specifications, images, price, stock, category, brand, attributes and SEO fields are each editable individually
Images and video can be added, reordered and given alt text
Regular price, sale price, compare at price and product cost are all recordable
Badges, featured flag, collection assignment and related products are set per product
Given a product is saved, when the storefront is reloaded, then the change is live immediately

title: Product content in both languages
narrative: As the store owner, I want to maintain the Arabic and English versions of a product separately, so that neither is a machine translation of the other.
ac: Product name, description and specifications are maintained independently in English and Arabic
The storefront shows the content for the active language
A product missing content in one language is reportable, so gaps can be found before launch

title: Product variants
narrative: As the store owner, I want each size and colour to have its own code, price and stock, so that the warehouse and the storefront agree.
scope: P1, with weight and dimensions at P1-L
ac: Variant attributes are definable per product
SKU, barcode, price and stock are held per variant
Weight and dimensions are recordable per variant
A variant with no stock behaves per US-04-03 on the storefront

title: Product cost captured from day one
narrative: As the store owner, I want cost recorded from the first day, so that margin reporting can later be built on real history rather than estimates.
ac: A cost field exists on every product and variant and is populated during catalogue load
Cost is visible only to roles with financial permission
Cost is imported by the migration tool where the source file carries it
Profitability and margin reporting itself is P2 and is not delivered here. The data it needs is

title: SEO fields per product
narrative: As the marketing team, I want to control how a product appears in search, so that the catalogue can be optimised without a developer.
ac: Slug, meta title, meta description, canonical and robots override are editable per product
The same fields are editable per category and per page
Changing a slug offers to create a redirect from the old one, per US-25-05

title: Bulk import and export
narrative: As the store owner, I want to move the catalogue in and out in bulk, so that I am never locked in.
ac: Products import in bulk through the tooling in Epic E23
Products export in bulk in the same mapped format
An export can be re imported without loss

title: Price and stock change history
narrative: As the store owner, I want to know who changed a price and when, so that a mistake can be found rather than argued about.
ac: Every price and stock change records the user, the previous value, the new value and the timestamp
The history is visible from the product
Bulk changes are recorded with the same detail per product

title: Categories, brands and collections
narrative: As the store owner, I want to organise the catalogue the way customers shop, so that browsing works.
trace: ADM-55, ADM-56, ADM-57, ENT-03, IA-03 to IA-05
ac: Categories and subcategories are managed with ordering, images and SEO fields
Brand pages carry a logo, description and SEO fields
Manually curated collections are created and ordered from admin
All three are maintained in both languages
Rules based automatic collections are not included, being P2

title: Stock levels
narrative: As the warehouse, I want on hand and available to be distinct numbers, so that I am not shipping stock that is already promised.
scope: P1, with reserved stock at P1-L, S2
ac: Stock on hand and stock available are both shown
Available stock reflects the reservation policy in force
Reserved stock tracking as a separate figure is second release. On hand and available are live at launch

title: Stock adjustments
narrative: As the warehouse, I want to correct stock with a reason attached, so that a discrepancy can be investigated later.
ac: Stock can be adjusted with a reason recorded
The user and timestamp are recorded with every adjustment
The adjustment is written to the audit log
A full inventory transaction record per movement is second release, per ENT-04

title: Low stock thresholds and alerts
narrative: As the store owner, I want to be told before something sells out, so that I can reorder in time.
ac: A low stock threshold can be set globally and overridden per SKU
Low and out of stock products appear in the Operations Console stock panel
The alert clears automatically when stock is replenished

title: Bulk stock import
narrative: As the store owner, I want to update stock from a file, so that a stock take is one upload.
ac: Stock quantities can be imported in bulk by SKU
The dry run in US-23-06 applies: the operator sees what will change before it changes
An unmatched SKU is reported rather than silently creating a product

title: Order search and filtering
narrative: As customer service, I want to find any order from whatever the customer tells me, so that the call is short.
ac: Orders are searchable and filterable by order number, customer, phone, email, status, payment state, date and carrier
Phone number search returns the order directly
Filters combine, and the resulting list can be saved as a view per US-15-05

title: Order detail
narrative: As customer service, I want everything about an order on one screen, so that I do not have to piece it together.
ac: The screen shows items, prices as charged, discounts, customer, address, payment, shipment, notes and a timeline
The timeline records every status change with actor and timestamp
Internal notes can be added and are never visible to the customer
Financial detail is visible only to roles with financial permission

title: Status updates
narrative: As the warehouse, I want to move an order forward, so that the customer sees progress.
ac: Status can be updated, with the transition validated against the status model
An invalid transition is refused with a reason
A status change that triggers a notification sends exactly one

title: Shipments from the order
narrative: As the warehouse, I want to create the shipment from the order, so that tracking is attached where it belongs.
ac: A shipment can be created and attached to the order with its tracking number
The tracking number is visible to the customer
A shipment can be corrected where the carrier returns a wrong code

title: Cancel an order
narrative: As customer service, I want to cancel with a reason, so that the record explains itself later.
ac: An order can be cancelled with a reason recorded
Cancellation releases reserved stock
Cancellation of a paid order does not by itself issue a refund: the refund is a separate, permissioned action

title: Invoices and packing slips
narrative: As the team, I want to print the paperwork, so that the parcel and the accounts are both correct.
ac: An invoice can be printed or downloaded from the order
A packing slip can be printed or downloaded
Both carry the legal entity details supplied under CR-12

title: Order export
narrative: As the store owner, I want orders in a spreadsheet, so that I can work outside the system when I need to.
ac: Orders export to a spreadsheet with selectable columns
The export honours the current filter
Exporting is permission controlled and is written to the audit log

title: Customer profile
narrative: As customer service, I want the customer history in front of me, so that I can help without asking them to repeat themselves.
ac: The profile shows contact details, addresses and order history
Returns and refunds against the customer are visible from the profile
Access is permission controlled, and the Marketing role cannot reach personal data beyond campaign needs

title: Internal notes on a customer
narrative: As customer service, I want to record context, so that the next person is not starting from nothing.
ac: Notes can be added to a customer record
Notes are never visible to the customer
Each note records its author and timestamp

title: Disable or suspend an account
narrative: As the store owner, I want to stop an abusive account, so that the store is protected.
ac: An account can be disabled or suspended with a reason recorded
A disabled account cannot sign in and is told to contact support
The action is permission controlled and written to the audit log

title: Customer metrics and export
narrative: As the store owner, I want spend and behaviour figures per customer, so that I can see who matters.
ac: Delivered in the second release. Profiles and order history are live at launch
Total spend, average order value, returns and coupon usage are shown per customer
Customer data export under privacy controls is delivered with it; at launch, requests are handled manually

title: Return case queue
narrative: As customer service, I want new return cases in a queue, so that none is forgotten.
ac: New return cases appear in a queue
The queue shows how long each case has been waiting
Pending returns also appear on the Operations Console

title: Review a return case
narrative: As customer service, I want the evidence and the order together, so that I can decide once.
ac: The case shows the reason, the description, the attached photographs and the order history together
The eligibility check result is shown, including the window used

title: Decide a return
narrative: As customer service, I want to approve, reject or partially approve with a recorded reason, so that the decision is defensible.
ac: A case can be approved, rejected or partially approved
A reason is recorded in every case, including approvals
The decision updates the return status visible to the customer and sends the notification
The decision is permission controlled and written to the audit log

title: Record receipt and condition
narrative: As the warehouse, I want to record what came back and in what state, so that the refund decision is informed.
scope: P1, with condition recording at P1-L
ac: Receipt of the returned item is recorded against the case
The condition of the returned item is recorded
Disposition handling, being return to stock, damaged or discard, is not included, being P2

title: Refund from the return case
narrative: As the accountant, I want to refund from the case with the reference captured, so that the money and the record match.
ac: A full or partial refund is initiated from the return case
The refund goes to the original payment method and the payment reference is recorded
The refund cannot exceed the amount actually paid after discount
The customer is notified with the amount and the reference

title: Return audit trail
narrative: As the owner, I want the whole case history preserved, so that a dispute has a record.
ac: Every action on the case is recorded with actor and timestamp
The trail includes the request, the decision, the receipt, the condition and the refund
The trail cannot be edited

title: Staff users and roles
narrative: As the owner, I want to give each person exactly the access their job needs, so that a mistake has a small blast radius.
ac: Staff users can be created and assigned one of the defined roles
Permissions are granular within the role definitions in Annex A Section B
No staff member receives full admin by default
Given a staff member without permission, when they attempt a refund, a price edit or a role change, then the action is refused and the attempt is recorded, per AC-11
The Accountant role has access to the Phase 1 financial operations at launch

title: Two factor authentication for admin
narrative: As the owner, I want a second factor on admin accounts, so that a stolen password is not enough.
ac: Two factor authentication is available for admin accounts
It can be required for the roles the owner chooses
Recovery from a lost second factor is documented and controlled

title: Audit log
narrative: As the owner, I want a searchable record of sensitive actions, so that a question about what happened has an answer.
trace: ADM-132, ADM-133, ADM-134, ROLE-10, ENT-17, MKT-25
scope: P1-L, with the deletion protection at P1
ac: Refunds, price changes, stock changes and permission changes are logged with actor, action, entity, before and after values, and timestamp
Logins and significant security events are recorded
The log is searchable by actor, entity, action and date
The audit trail cannot be deleted from the interface by ordinary users
Third party administrative actions appear in the same log
The reduced boundary is explicit: forensic reporting and log analytics are not included

title: Nothing a customer reads is locked in code
narrative: As the store owner, I want every storefront text, image and link editable from admin, so that the store is mine to change.
ac: Every text, image and link a customer can see is editable from admin
No customer facing string requires a code change to correct
The client, unaided, edits a product and a storefront section, and both changes appear correctly on the English and the Arabic storefront, per AC-20

title: Home page sections
narrative: As the store owner, I want to run the home page, so that the front of the store follows the season.
ac: Section content, images, calls to action and links are editable
The order of sections is changeable
Changes are independent per language

title: Show and hide sections
narrative: As the store owner, I want to switch a section off without losing it, so that a seasonal block can return next year.
ac: Any home page section can be hidden and shown again
Hiding a section does not delete its content
A hidden section leaves no gap on the storefront

title: Category and brand page content
narrative: As the marketing team, I want each category and brand to have its own presentation, so that the store does not look generic.
ac: Banner, description and hero imagery are editable per category
Brand page content is editable per brand
Both are maintained in both languages

title: Collection content and ordering
narrative: As the merchandiser, I want to control what is in a collection and in what order, so that the best product is first.
ac: Products can be added to and removed from a collection
Product order within the collection is set manually and is respected on the storefront
Collection page content is editable in both languages

title: Navigation and footer
narrative: As the store owner, I want to change the menu and the footer, so that a new category is reachable the day it exists.
ac: Header navigation and mega menu structure are managed from admin
Footer content, links and columns are managed from admin
Both are maintained in both languages, and a link missing in one language is reported

title: Static and policy pages
narrative: As the store owner, I want to change policy text myself, so that a legal update is not a development task.
ac: Static pages, policy pages and the FAQ are editable without code
Edits are independent per language
The return policy page and the configured return window stay consistent, per US-13-02

title: Promotional banners and campaign pages
narrative: As the marketing team, I want to build an offer page, so that a campaign does not need a release.
ac: Promotional banners can be created, scheduled, targeted to a page and removed
A campaign or offer landing page can be created from the existing components without a developer
Campaign pages exist in both languages
The boundary is explicit: creating an entirely new type of page layout or component that does not exist in the design system is a Change Request

title: Content maintained independently in both languages
narrative: As the store owner, I want the Arabic store to be genuinely Arabic, so that it does not read as a translation of an English page.
ac: Every editable content area is maintained separately in English and Arabic
Editing one language never overwrites the other
Missing content in one language is reportable before launch

title: Preview before publish
narrative: As the store owner, I want to see a change before customers do, so that a mistake is caught privately.
ac: Any content change can be previewed as it will appear
Preview covers both languages
A previewed change is not visible to customers until it is published

title: Revert a content change
narrative: As the store owner, I want to undo a content edit, so that a bad change is recoverable.
ac: A content change can be reverted to its previous version
The revert is recorded with actor and timestamp

title: File formats accepted
narrative: As the store owner, I want the tool to read what Amazon actually gives me, so that I am not reformatting files first.
ac: CSV, tab delimited and Excel files are accepted
An unsupported file is refused with a clear explanation, not a stack trace
A very large file is accepted and processed per US-23-08

title: Encoding detection verified against Arabic
narrative: As the store owner, I want Arabic to survive the import, so that the catalogue is not corrupted on arrival.
ac: Character encoding is detected automatically
Given a file containing Arabic product text in the encoding Amazon commonly produces, when it is imported, then the Arabic text is stored and displayed correctly
Given encoding cannot be determined confidently, when the file is uploaded, then the operator is asked rather than a guess being applied silently

title: Column mapping
narrative: As the store owner, I want to tell the tool what each column means, so that it works with any file, not one report format.
scope: P1, with brand mapping at P1-L
ac: Each column in the source file is mapped to a store field through an interface
Source attributes are mappable to store attributes
A category mapping table can be built and is reusable
An unmapped required field blocks the import with a clear message

title: Saved mapping profiles
narrative: As the store owner, I want to map once and reuse it, so that the second import is faster than the first.
ac: A mapping can be saved with a name and reused on a later import
A saved mapping applied to a file with different columns reports the mismatch rather than importing wrongly

title: Preview
narrative: As the store owner, I want to see the first rows interpreted, so that I catch a mapping error before it matters.
ac: The first rows are shown as they will be interpreted, before anything is written
The preview shows the mapped field names, not the raw column headers

title: Dry run
narrative: As the store owner, I want a full report of what would happen, so that I never find out by breaking the catalogue.
scope: P1, with per field overwrite control at P1-L
ac: A dry run produces a validation report listing what will be created, what will be updated, and what will fail and why
Nothing is written to the catalogue during a dry run
The operator can control which fields an update is permitted to overwrite
The report is downloadable

title: Product variations
narrative: As the store owner, I want parent and child listings to become proper variable products, so that the storefront shows sizes rather than duplicates.
ac: Parent and child listings in the source file are converted into variable products with variants
Variant attributes, SKU, price and stock are populated from the source
A child row whose parent is missing is reported as an error rather than imported as a standalone product

title: Background processing
narrative: As the store owner, I want a big import to finish, so that the catalogue load is not a series of failures.
ac: Imports run in the background and do not fail on large files
Progress is visible while the import runs
An interrupted import can be resumed or safely re run per US-23-09

title: Safe re runs
narrative: As the store owner, I want to run the same file again safely, so that keeping the catalogue current is routine.
ac: Given a file that has already been imported, when it is imported again, then existing products are updated by SKU and no duplicates are created
The behaviour holds for variable products as well as simple products
The client re runs the tool on a changed file at the Stage 5 gate and confirms it updates rather than duplicates

title: Error report
narrative: As the store owner, I want to fix the rows that failed, so that a partial import is not a dead end.
ac: A row level error report is downloadable after every import
Each error names the row, the field and the reason
The corrected file can be re uploaded and imported

title: Import history
narrative: As the store owner, I want to know what was imported and by whom, so that an unexpected change can be traced.
ac: Every import run records the file, the mapping used, row counts, the outcome, the actor and the timestamp
The history is visible in admin
Import undo and scheduled recurring imports are not included, being P2

title: Fields imported and export
narrative: As the store owner, I want the data that matters to come across, and to be able to take it out again.
trace: MIG-13, MIG-14, MIG-15, MIG-16, MIG-17, MIG-25
scope: P1, with SEO fields, images and generated alt text at P1-L
ac: Price, sale price and cost are imported
Stock quantity is imported
SEO fields are imported where present
Images are downloaded and stored on the store server, subject to the rights confirmation at CR-08
Alt text is generated from the product title where none is supplied
The catalogue exports in the same mapped format

title: Dashboard figures
narrative: As the store owner, I want the headline numbers on opening the admin, so that I know how the business is doing.
trace: ADM-01 to ADM-04, ADM-08, ADM-09, ADM-15
scope: P1, with average order value and charts at P1-L
ac: Revenue, orders, units sold and average order value are shown
Charts are available by day, week, month and a custom range
Top products are listed
Quick actions for adding a product, creating a coupon and viewing pending orders are present
Figures reconcile with the sales report for the same period

title: Operational panels on the dashboard
narrative: As the store owner, I want problems surfaced rather than found, so that the dashboard is useful rather than decorative.
scope: P1, with the refunds and returns panel at P1-L
ac: Low stock, out of stock, orders requiring action and pending returns and refunds are all visible
Each links to the screen where the work is done

title: Sales report
narrative: As the accountant, I want the sales figures broken down, so that I can reconcile them.
ac: Revenue, net sales, orders, units, average order value, discounts and shipping are reported
The report is filterable by date range
The report is exportable
