Access is limited to roles with financial permission

title: Inventory report
narrative: As the store owner, I want stock health in one report, so that purchasing decisions have a basis.
ac: Low stock, out of stock, dead stock and adjustments are reported
The report is filterable and exportable

title: Funnel and traffic reporting
narrative: As the marketing team, I want the funnel and the traffic sources, so that spend can be judged.
scope: P1-L, delivered through the analytics platform
ac: Session to product to cart to checkout to purchase is measurable in the analytics platform
Traffic by channel, source and campaign is measurable
Conversion rate is available through the analytics platform rather than as an admin figure at launch
The event set in Epic E26 is what makes this true, and is verified with it

title: Second release reports
narrative: As the store owner, I want to know exactly which reports arrive after launch, so that their absence is not a surprise.
ac: The product performance report, the search terms report, the dashboard customer figures and customer lifetime metrics are delivered in the second release
The data those reports need is captured from launch, so that they are built on real history

title: Measurement and advertising tags
epicname: MARKETING ENABLEMENT, SEO AND THIRD PARTY ACCESS
narrative: As the marketing team, I want the tracking in place on day one, so that launch traffic is measurable.
ac: Google Analytics 4 and Tag Manager are installed with the full ecommerce event set
The Meta pixel is installed
The TikTok pixel is installed with standard ecommerce events
Events fire correctly in both languages and are verified before launch
Which advertising platforms are live at launch follows the client decision at OD-21

title: Product feeds
epicname: MARKETING ENABLEMENT, SEO AND THIRD PARTY ACCESS
narrative: As the media buyer, I want product feeds, so that dynamic retargeting and shopping listings are possible at all.
ac: A Meta product catalogue feed is produced and validates against the platform requirements
A Google Merchant Center feed is produced and validates
Feeds refresh on a schedule and reflect current price and availability
A product excluded from advertising can be excluded from the feed

title: Campaign attribution through to the order
epicname: MARKETING ENABLEMENT, SEO AND THIRD PARTY ACCESS
narrative: As the store owner, I want revenue attributable to a campaign, so that advertising spend can be judged on sales rather than clicks.
ac: Campaign tracking parameters are preserved from landing through to the order record
The order record carries the attribution data
Attribution survives a guest checkout and a sign in during checkout

title: Consent management
epicname: MARKETING ENABLEMENT, SEO AND THIRD PARTY ACCESS
narrative: As the store owner, I want tracking to respect consent, so that measurement does not create a legal problem.
ac: A cookie and consent banner is present and configurable
Tracking is consent aware: tags respect the recorded consent state
Consent choices are recorded

title: Redirect manager
epicname: MARKETING ENABLEMENT, SEO AND THIRD PARTY ACCESS
narrative: As the marketing team, I want to create redirects myself, so that a changed URL does not lose its traffic.
scope: P1, with the missing page log at P1-L
ac: Permanent redirects are created from admin without a developer
A redirect loop or a redirect to a missing page is refused with an explanation
Missing page errors are logged and visible in admin

title: Technical SEO foundations
epicname: MARKETING ENABLEMENT, SEO AND THIRD PARTY ACCESS
narrative: As the marketing team, I want the technical basics correct, so that the store can rank.
trace: MKT-12, MKT-15, MKT-16, MKT-17, MKT-18, NFR-03, ADM-38 to ADM-41
ac: Clean URLs, meta titles and descriptions, canonical tags, breadcrumbs and alt text are in place
An XML sitemap and a robots file are produced and controllable from admin
Structured data for product, organisation and breadcrumbs is emitted and validates
Search Console and Bing Webmaster verification are in place
hreflang tags target the English and Arabic versions of each page correctly

title: Third party access controls
epicname: MARKETING ENABLEMENT, SEO AND THIRD PARTY ACCESS
narrative: As the store owner, I want an agency to be unable to break the store, so that marketing help does not become a maintenance problem.
trace: MKT-21, MKT-22, MKT-23, MKT-24, MKT-25, ROLE-05
scope: P1, with the personal data limit, staging access and audit visibility at P1-L
ac: The Marketing role cannot install software, edit templates or edit files
The Marketing role cannot reach customer personal data beyond campaign needs
Tracking scripts are deployed through Google Tag Manager, and no third party edits site code directly
Third parties receive staging access for testing before any production change
Every third party administrative action appears in the audit log

title: Third Party Access Protocol
epicname: MARKETING ENABLEMENT, SEO AND THIRD PARTY ACCESS
narrative: As the store owner, I want a document I can hand to an agency, so that the rules are agreed before access is given.
ac: A short written protocol is delivered, stating the role granted, the Tag Manager rule, the change request rule, the notification duty and the chargeability of repairing third party damage
It is issued in a form the client can forward to an agency directly

title: Standard ecommerce event set
narrative: As the marketing team, I want the whole funnel instrumented, so that every step can be measured.
trace: EVT-01 to EVT-09, EVT-11 to EVT-14, EVT-16
ac: Events fire for home page viewed, item list viewed, search, product viewed, product card clicked, add to wishlist, add to cart, remove from cart and cart viewed
Events fire for begin checkout, add shipping info, add payment info and purchase
The purchase event carries items, tax, shipping and discount values
Registration and login events fire
Every event fires once per occurrence, with no duplicate on a page refresh

title: Secondary events
narrative: As the marketing team, I want coupon, refund, return and zero result events, so that the less obvious behaviour is also measurable.
ac: Coupon applied, refund issued, zero result search and return requested events fire
Promotion viewed and promotion clicked events are not included, being P2

title: Event tracking plan
narrative: As the store owner, I want a document defining every event, so that a number in a report can be traced to its source.
ac: The plan defines every event, its trigger, its parameters, and the source of truth for each business metric
Every event in the plan is verified as firing correctly before launch
The plan is delivered in writing as part of the Stage 1 technical design
The reduced boundary is explicit: a bespoke custom event plan beyond the standard set is not included

title: Mobile first and responsive
narrative: As a shopper on a phone, I want the store designed for my screen, so that mobile is not an afterthought.
ac: Every screen is responsive across phone, tablet and desktop
Testing begins on mobile rather than being a later phase
Every screen is verified in both languages at every breakpoint

title: Performance
narrative: As a shopper, I want pages to load quickly, so that I do not leave before I have seen anything.
ac: Images are optimised and lazy loaded
Caching and a content delivery network are in place
Performance is measured on the staging environment before launch and the results are recorded
No performance, conversion, traffic or ranking outcome is warranted, per EX-31

title: Security
narrative: As the store owner, I want current security practice applied throughout, so that the store is not an easy target.
ac: HTTPS throughout, secure password storage, role based access control, admin protection, input validation, rate limiting, secret management and dependency updates are all in place
No card data is stored, and the provider secure integration pattern is followed
The security controls are listed in the handover documentation
No guarantee of immunity from all future vulnerabilities is given or implied

title: Data integrity
narrative: As the store owner, I want money, stock and orders to stay consistent, so that a concurrent action never corrupts a record.
ac: Payment, order and inventory operations are transactionally safe
Duplicate protection holds across payments, orders and inventory
Concurrent purchases of the last unit of stock result in one sale, not two
Automated tests cover pricing, promotions, refunds, stock and duplicate order protection, per the reduced scope at DOD-04

title: Backups and environments
narrative: As the store owner, I want a tested way back, so that a bad change is recoverable.
ac: Database and media backups run to the agreed retention
The restore procedure is documented and has been performed at least once, not only written
Development, staging and production environments exist, and risky changes are never tested on the live site
A rollback procedure is documented and tested before go live

title: Observability
narrative: As the store owner, I want to know when something is failing, so that a problem is found before a customer reports it.
ac: Application logs, error monitoring, integration logs and admin audit logs are in place
Integration failures against the payment and carrier providers are visible without reading a server log

title: Accessibility
narrative: As any visitor, I want the store to be usable without a mouse and readable at normal contrast, so that it does not exclude people unnecessarily.
ac: Keyboard usability, form labels, colour contrast, image alt text and semantic structure are implemented
The core purchase path is completable using a keyboard alone
The reduced boundary is explicit: this is the accessibility scope recorded at NFR-11, not certification against a named standard

title: Privacy
narrative: As the store owner, I want consent and data handling correct, so that the store is defensible under Egyptian data protection law.
scope: P1, with automated request handling at P1-L, S2
ac: Consent is captured, the privacy policy is published, and data minimisation is applied
Marketing consent is separate from account creation
Automated data export and deletion request handling is second release. At launch, requests are handled manually
The hosting location decision and any authorisation it requires are the client responsibility, per R-03 and OD-27

title: Browser support and scalability
narrative: As the store owner, I want the store to work on what customers use and to cope with growth, so that success is not a failure mode.
ac: Current Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox, plus mobile browsers, are supported and tested
The platform is provisioned against the stated assumption of up to 5,000 products and 300 orders per day, with headroom for short campaign peaks
Growth beyond that is absorbed by resizing infrastructure rather than re implementing the core, bounded by FIX-10
No guarantee is given that a future P2 or P3 capability can be added without redesign

title: Pre development deliverables
narrative: As the store owner, I want the design and the plan in writing before code is written, so that I am approving something I can see.
ac: The technical design and architecture document, the technology stack proposal with reasoning and expected operating cost, the sitemap, user flows, wireframes and interface design, the milestone breakdown, and the integrations list with the accounts and costs required from the client are all delivered
This specification and the Feature Register together satisfy PRE-06
The store operations walkthrough is performed on the actual admin environment, with the Annex A Section G10 list reviewed together and confirmed, before development begins
The canonical design source is English, and the Arabic layouts are the right to left localisation of that approved design, not a separate design

title: Handover deliverables
narrative: As the store owner, I want to own everything at the end, so that another team could take this over.
trace: HND-01, HND-02, HND-03, HND-04, HND-05, HND-06, HND-07, HND-08, HND-09, HND-10, HND-11, HND-12
ac: Source code is in a repository the client owns, with a clear development history
Design source files, the design system and assets are delivered
Documentation covers setup, deployment, environment variables and integrations, and includes an Arabic administrator guide covering the English interface
Domain, DNS, hosting and cloud access are in the client name
Database schema, migrations, and backup and restore instructions are delivered
Payment, shipping, email and analytics accounts are under client ownership
The staging environment, test cases and acceptance results are delivered
Production deployment and a documented rollback procedure are delivered

The admin training session, the credentials handover and a known issues list are delivered. Training is the written Arabic administrator manual plus a live handover session, at the reduced scope recorded at HND-09
The warranty period for defect correction runs from Production Go-Live, separate from new features, on the terms in the Services Agreement
The Third Party Access Protocol is delivered, per US-25-08
The Event Tracking Plan is delivered, per US-26-03
